body.statement: Under Assumptions \(\ref{ass:iid-sampling}\), \(\ref{ass:holder-regressions}\), \(\ref{ass:design-density}\), \(\ref{ass:characteristic-kernels}\), and \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\), there is \(K<\infty\) such that, with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), all \(d2^{d-1}\) risks and all \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) score-relevant residual-HSIC values lie in their cross-fitted bands, with \(w_R\le K\{\sqrt{\log(M_d/\alpha)/n}+a_n^2\}\) and \(w_H\le K\{\sqrt{\log(M_d/\alpha)/n}+a_n\}\). Boundedness of the kernels controls the held-out empirical fluctuation in \(w_H\), while Assumption \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\) is used only to convert the cross-fitted residual error into the additive \(a_n\) term. On this event, if \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\), every queried HSIC value belongs to \(\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)\), \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\), and \(2w_H<\lambda\), then \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_n=\{G_0\}\). Without the two separation inequalities, interval propagation never forces a binary label for an HSIC interval meeting both \(0\) and \([\lambda,\infty)\): it retains both labels and returns the union of all compatible terminal DAGs, which may be a singleton or may contain multiple graphs.
body.justification: The finite-sample theorem ties singleton recovery to the primitive gain slack and an explicit pruning resolution while preserving abstention near the discontinuity at independence.
body.gap: Pfister et al. (2018, Theorem E.2 and Proposition E.3) and Shekhar et al. (2023, Theorems 6 and 7) do not jointly cover learned normalized risks, simultaneous residual perturbations, adaptive insertions, and separated-model graph confidence sets.
body.consumer: Users receive a certified labelled DAG only when both navigation and pruning margins dominate propagated uncertainty.
body.proof_tex:
All coordinates and all residuals are bounded because \(\mathcal X\) is compact.  We first record a regression construction.  If \(|A|=m\le d-1\), partition the compact rectangle \(\mathcal X_A\) into cubes of side \(h\) and use, on each cube, polynomials of total degree two, clipped to the outcome range.  Taylor's formula and Assumption \(\ref{ass:holder-regressions}\) give a sieve element \(g_h\) with
\[
 \|g_h-\mu_{v,A}\|_\infty\le K_0h^3,
\]
while the sieve dimension is at most \(K_1h^{-m}\).  For bounded squared loss, the basic inequality for empirical least squares, followed by Bernstein's inequality on a Euclidean net of this finite-dimensional clipped sieve, gives, conditionally on a training fold and with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\[
 \|\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\|_{L^2(P_A)}^2
 \le K_2\left\{h^6+\frac{h^{-m}\log(L/\delta)}{n}\right\}. \tag{10}
\]
Here \(L\) is the number of regressions fitted simultaneously; the density bounds ensure that the same constants work on nonempty design cells, while empty cells carry no \(P_A\)-risk.  To see the fast rather than square-root stochastic term in (10), apply Bernstein to the loss difference: its variance is bounded by a constant times its mean excess risk because the responses and candidates are bounded.  Peeling the net by excess-risk shells and summing the resulting geometric probabilities proves (10).

Choose \(h=\{\log(M_d/\alpha)/n\}^{1/(m+6)}\), use the largest dimension \(m=d-1\), and absorb fold-size constants into \(K\).  A union bound over the \(d2^{d-1}\) regressions yields
\[
 \max_{v,A}\|\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\|_{L^2(P_A)}
 \le K a_n. \tag{11}
\]
For the finitely many small \(n\) for which the chosen sieve has fewer than one effective cell, clipping and a larger \(K\) give the same inequality.

On a held-out fold, define \(\widehat R_{v,A}\) as the average squared residual formed with the off-fold fit.  Conditional on that fit, orthogonality of conditional expectation gives
\[
 \mathbb E[(V_v-\widehat\mu_{v,A}(V_A))^2\mid\widehat\mu_{v,A}]
 =R_{v,A}+\|\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\|_{L^2(P_A)}^2. \tag{12}
\]
Hoeffding's inequality for bounded held-out losses, a union bound, (11), and (12) produce simultaneous intervals containing every \(R_{v,A}\) with half-width
\[
 w_R\le K\left\{\sqrt{\frac{\log(M_d/\alpha)}n}+a_n^2\right\}. \tag{13}
\]

Next compute bounded-kernel HSIC as its usual centered order-four V-statistic on a held-out fold.  Replacing one held-out observation changes it by at most \(K/n\), so the bounded-difference inequality and a union bound give fluctuation at most \(K\sqrt{\log(M_d/\alpha)/n}\).  Its diagonal V-statistic bias is \(O(n^{-1})\), which is absorbed by this term.  If \(e_i\) and \(\widehat e_i\) are the true and fitted residuals, Assumption \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\), telescoping the finite product of kernel factors, and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 |\operatorname{HSIC}(\widehat e,V_u)-\operatorname{HSIC}(e,V_u)|
 \le K\mathbb E|\widehat e-e|
 \le K\|\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\|_{L^2(P_A)}.
\]
Together with (11), this gives simultaneous score-relevant HSIC bands with
\[
 w_H\le K\left\{\sqrt{\frac{\log(M_d/\alpha)}n}+a_n\right\}. \tag{14}
\]
The same construction is made for the pruning functionals \(H(v,A,u)\) with \(u\notin A\).  There are at most another \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) of them; replacing \(M_d\) by at most \(2M_d\) changes only the universal multiplicative constant in (13)--(14), since \(\log(2M_d/\alpha)\le2\log(M_d/\alpha)\).  Thus every adaptively queried pruning value is covered on the same event.

Suppose now that all queried HSIC values lie in \(\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)\) and \(2w_H<\lambda\).  If the true value is zero, coverage implies that the interval's upper endpoint is below \(\lambda\); if it is at least \(\lambda\), the lower endpoint is strictly positive.  Hence every set-valued decision is the correct singleton.  In particular, the discontinuous indicator is used only after separation; when an interval meets both regions Definition \(\ref{def:simultaneous-bands}\) retains both labels.

Under singleton dependence decisions, interval arithmetic applied to Definitions \(\ref{def:correlation-ratio}\)--\(\ref{def:insertion-gain}\) contains every true gain, because Assumption \(\ref{ass:variance-nondegeneracy}\) keeps all variance denominators away from zero.  At any non-topological order, Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) supplies a correcting gain at least \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\).  Every score table compatible with the bands assigns that same gain a value at least \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}-2w_S>0\).  Strict ascent on the finite permutation set therefore makes every compatible terminal order topological.  The singleton pruning decisions are exactly those in Theorem \(\ref{thm:oracle-recovery}\), so every compatible terminal DAG equals \(G_0\).  Their union is \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_n=\{G_0\}\).

If a band meets both \(0\) and \([\lambda,\infty)\), the construction records both labels (and also does so after an empty intersection), so it never converts proximity to the discontinuity into a false binary assertion.  Taking the union over all compatible paths proves the final, deliberately set-valued conclusion.  Such a union can still be a singleton if the ambiguous functional is irrelevant to every terminal pruning decision; therefore no unconditional multiplicity claim is made.
